To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TRAFD-1, a previously unappreciated regulator of toll-like receptor signaling, interacts with the large, multi-modu-lar adapter protein Plekhm1 to regulate osteoclast acidifica-tion and resorption.
TRAFD1 interacts with Plekhm-1 and is required for vesicle trafficking and acidification in osteoclast resorption.
TRAFD 1 is a new interaction partner of Plekhm 1 and regulates acidification and resorption of osteoclasts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the bone resorptive process by the osteoclast.
the molecular mechanisms of bone homeostasis, particularly in the regulation of the osteoclast.
the identification of a new protein that regulates osteoclast function, and the elucidation of a new pathway in osteoclast biology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TRAFD is a novel regulator of osteoclast function that acts via the late endosomal/lysosomal pathway.
TRAFD is a novel regulator of the osteoclast acidifying machinery, and that TRAFD and PLEKHm1 are key partners in this process.
TRAFD is a novel regulator of osteoclast function and bone homeostasis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adapter protein TRAFD1 is required for vesicle trafficking in osteoclast acid secretion and resorption.
TRAFD is a new partner for Plekhm1, and that the interaction of these proteins with Rab7 is required for the normal function of Plekhm in osteoclast acid secretion and bone resorption.
TRAFD 1 is a novel Plekhm1-interacting protein that regulates osteoclast vesicular trafficking, acidification and resorption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TRAFD is a new interaction partner of Plekhm that is important for osteoclast acid secretion.
TRAFD is a new interaction partner for Plekhm1, and that TRAFD regulates osteoclast acid secretion.
